land.text: the Chola country on the Kaveri, which the Kalabhras 'invaded Tamil country, displaced the existing kingdoms and ruled'

successors.note: The Chola dynasty page says the Cholas 'disappeared from the Tamil land almost completely in this debacle' and had to wait until Vijayalaya in the ninth century; the Kalabhra dossier is written by another part of sa-02. No state holds the Kaveri country in Cliopatria between 306 and 849.

capitals.name: Uraiyur (Tiruchirappalli)
capitals.note: 'Urayur (now a part of Thiruchirapalli) was their oldest capital'; 'Kaveripattinam also served as an early Chola capital' (Poompuhar, about 79.85 E, 11.15 N); neither is dated. Coordinates are the gazetteer's Tiruchirappalli.

keyframe_review.note: 28,900 km2 for -291..298 (Kaveri valley, 76.7-79.9 E, 10.2-11.4 N: Uraiyur, Karur, Coimbatore and the coast at Kaveripattinam). The page gives no area and no extent ('the Chola country watered by the river Kaveri'). Ok for -291..179; from c. 180 the Kongu part (44 cells) goes to the Cheras, see the next keyframe. The Maurya Empire page puts the Cholas among the neighbours 'beyond the borders' of Ashoka, not subject to him; Cliopatria's Maurya shape touches this one until -226, and the Maurya dossier now excludes Tamil Nadu.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 180..298: the Chera page puts the capital Vanchi-Karuvur (Karur) in the Kongu country and says that under Chenguttuvan (c. 180 CE) 'Chera territory covered the Malabar Coast and the Kongu country'. Cliopatria gives Karur and Coimbatore to the Cholas throughout, which conflicts with the Chera page. The page gives no date for the Chola loss; c. 180 is the Chera page's date for the king.

keyframe_review.note: Same outline as -291 (28,900 km2) for 299..305; Kongu removed as for 180..298. The split at 299 is not explained by any page opened; the Chola dynasty page puts the end of the Sangam age at 'c. 300'.

region.text: the Chola country watered by the river Kaveri, with Uraiyur

ledger.note: The Cholas exist by 291 BCE. The page is silent on a founding: 'The earliest datable references to the Chola are from inscriptions dated to the 3rd century BCE during the reign of Ashoka' (Ashokan Edicts 'inscribed 273 BCE-232 BCE'), as southern neighbours on friendly terms. The year is Cliopatria's first shape (the Sangam age is dated 'c. 600 BCE' and 'late centuries before the common era' on the same page); the Early Cholas page gives the same Ashokan dates.

region.text: the Kongu country (Karur and Coimbatore), land that Cliopatria's Early Cholas shape holds and that the Chera page puts in 'Chera territory' under Chenguttuvan, c. 180 CE

ledger.note: c. 180: Kongu passes to the Cheras. Chera page: Chenguttuvan 'c. 180 CE' (or 'either the first or the last quarter of the second century CE'); under him 'Chera territory covered the Malabar Coast and the Kongu country'. The counterpart is my reading: Cliopatria holds Karur and Coimbatore in the Chola shape.

region.text: the Chola country at the end of the Sangam age

ledger.note: c. 305: the Early Cholas end. The page is silent on the date: it puts the end of the Sangam age at 'c. 300', says the Kalabhras 'invaded Tamil country, displaced the existing kingdoms' without a date, and that the Cholas 'disappeared from the Tamil land almost completely in this debacle'. The year is Cliopatria's last shape.

certainty.note: The Sangam kingdoms have no recorded frontiers; the Chola country is 'watered by the river Kaveri' on the pages. Kongu changes hands in the Chera page's account, not in the Chola pages.

sources.title: Early Cholas
sources.note: Ashokan mention (273-232 BCE), Karikala c. 90 BCE, Duttha Gamini and Ellalan, capitals; no area, no end date.

sources.title: Chola dynasty
sources.note: Earliest datable references, Sangam period, Ellalan 235 BCE, capitals Uraiyur and Kaveripattinam, Kalabhra debacle, Vijayalaya 848.

sources.title: Chera dynasty
sources.note: Third page, opened for the Chera dossier and cited here for the Kongu country and Karur under the Cheras (c. 180).

notes:
Group sa-02-a. Pages: Early Cholas, Chola dynasty, plus the Chera dynasty page (opened for the Chera dossier) for the one Kongu event; one more than the 1-2 page budget.

THIN BY NECESSITY. The pages date nothing about Chola territory: no area, no frontier, no year for the founding or the end. The founding and end events are confidence 1 (Cliopatria's -291 and 305); the first datable fact is Ashoka's edicts (273-232 BCE) naming the Cholas as friendly neighbours, not subjects (Maurya page: 'Bindusara did not conquer the friendly Tamil kingdoms of the Cholas ... Pandyas, and Cheras').

UNDATED, NOT ENTERED. (1) Karikala (c. 90 BCE on the Early Cholas page; 'c. 110 CE (traditional)' on the Chola invasion of Sri Lanka page) 'broke the confederacy that was formed against him and established hegemony over Pandyas and Cheras': no date for the hegemony, so no vassal events. (2) The Mahavamsa's Chola prince Ellalan took Rajarata 'in 235 BCE' on the Chola page, 205 BC on the Anuradhapura page; he is treated in the Anuradhapura dossier as a usurper of Chola origin, not an occupation by the Chola state. (3) The Kalabhra date: 'sometime between the 3rd century and 6th century CE', earliest inscription 270 CE (Kalabhra page, not opened for this dossier).

CONFLICT WITH THE CHERA PAGE. Cliopatria's shape holds Karur and Coimbatore; the Chera page has Karur (Vanchi-Karuvur) as a Chera capital and Kongu in Chera territory c. 180. The Chera dossier gains it and this one loses it at 180; a reviewer who prefers Cliopatria can delete both events and keyframes.

GAZETTEER. Kongu is described by Karur and Coimbatore radii; a 'Kongu' region entry would fit. Kaveripattinam (Poompuhar) and Uraiyur are not gazetteer places.
